source: User photographed Croatian edition Notes pages XV/XVI and confirmed answers in chat, 2026-10-16. Photographs remain private; only derived rules saved in GitHub.

rules.bare_destination: When a separately printed marginal row omits a book abbreviation, use the source page's Bible book as destination book. Inside one semicolon-separated physical row, an omitted book after an explicit book abbreviation inherits the most recent explicit destination book on that row, not the source book. Never inherit a target book from a different physical row.
rules.equals_marker: Printed '=' preceding a cross-reference denotes a literary doublet or parallel in the SAME biblical book (edition explanation paragraph 2). It is a relation marker, not a destination verse or a missing book abbreviation. Preserve it separately; resolve bare coordinate to source page book.
rules.double_bar_marker: Printed '||' denotes parallel corresponding passages in DIFFERENT books. Preserve as relation marker; do not use it to determine source chapter or verse.
rules.arrow_marker: Printed arrow ↗ denotes scriptural quotation, especially older scripture cited by a newer book, per explanation paragraph 3. Store marker as metadata, independent of destination coordinates.
rules.no_prefix_marker: Printed citation without a preceding relation marker is an ordinary helpful reference.
rules.comma_verses: Comma-separated distinct verse numbers under a chapter are independent destination link records, e.g. Si 43 6,7 -> Sir 43:6 and Sir 43:7.
rules.semicolon_chapters: Each semicolon-separated chapter or chapter/verse is an independent link record; e.g. Ps 8; 104 -> one chapter-level link to Ps 8 and one to Ps 104.
rules.suffix_s: Edition paragraph 5: 's' applies to the named line and the following lines/verses. Preserve literally; do not fabricate an end verse.
rules.suffix_p: Edition paragraph 5: 'p' points to a parallel passage. Preserve literally; do not fabricate an end verse.
rules.suffix_plus: Edition paragraph 4: '+' indicates a useful further reference or explanatory note, often at the referenced place. Preserve literally; do not create another destination solely because of '+'.
rules.missing_book_ocr: When OCR reads incomplete abbreviations, e.g. 'Ch 1 1-4' or 's 14 14+', make tentative corrections (1 Ch -> 1Chr, Is -> Isa) if consistent with visible context and catalog. Keep original print, record assumption and quality flag. No need to ask human to check every occurrence.
rules.layout_groups: Edition paragraph 7: a printed marginal note may appear BELOW its actual source line when the margin is occupied; blank lines ordinarily separate groups of notes that refer to distinct main-text lines. Therefore a strict nearest-y verse matcher alone is not safe. Capture original reference grouping, separator/gap positions, and reconcile with main-text verse spans.
rules.book_page: Source book is established for the scanned page, not redetected for each marginal note.
rules.running_header: On left book pages upper-left chapter/verse may indicate FIRST verse; on right book pages upper-right may indicate LAST verse. Verify physical page side and role.
rules.review_policy: Do not ask for thousands of manual checks. Flag assumptions in machine-readable metadata and quantify accuracy against independent human-verified scan samples; isolate only genuine layout/cut-off exceptions.

confirmed_versus_estimated_accuracy: Rules confirmed; 99%+ whole-pipeline performance NOT YET demonstrated.
